messages:
nicole: Heads-up: we're seeing intermittent 1-4% packet loss on east-west traffic inside the x2dn GPU fleet (us-west-2). Affected nodes: gpu-x2dn-03/07/11. Symptoms: RDMA/GPUDirect jobs fail with transport errors, TCP retransmits spike, and sometimes the interface flaps briefly. Noticed after the last ENA driver rollout earlier today.

ops-bot: deploy:ena-driver v2.4.8 rolled to x2dn pool at 02:43 UTC (canary -> batch).

sam: Thanks. Any kernel logs / ethtool stats? Does the flap show as link down or just rx/tx errors?

nicole: Mostly no full link down, just massive RX/TX counters going nonzero then back. Pasting `ethtool -S` excerpt from gpu-x2dn-03 (trimmed):

```
eth0_rx_no_buf: 152
eth0_rx_missed_errors: 108
eth0_tx_aborted_errors: 22
eth0_rx_no_desc: 0
eth0_rx_dropped: 115
```

Also dmesg shows repeated ena warnings: `ena 0000:00:04.0: ena_com_adminq_submit_cmd timed out` and `ENA: Rx ring overflow`.

kai: That `ena_com_adminq_submit_cmd timed out` looks like firmware/queue starvation. Can you confirm ENA firmware version? `ethtool -i eth0` output?

nicole: `driver: ena, version: 2.4.8, firmware-version: 1.9.0`

lina: Quick mitigation: try disabling GRO and LRO on a single affected host and run a canary workload. `sudo ethtool -K eth0 gro off lro off gso off` — that helped with similar bursts on p4d last year. Also try reducing MTU from 9000 -> 8900 in case jumbo packets are getting split weirdly across the vSwitch/firmware.

sam: Agree. Also check `sysctl net.core.netdev_max_backlog` and `rx_ring` sizes. If adminq is getting overwhelmed, bumping ring sizes or reducing batching can help temporarily.

nicole: Will run the two quick ones now on gpu-x2dn-03 only (canary).

[~5m later]

nicole: Can confirm: after `ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off` and MTU 8900, observed RX errors dropped to single-digit and RDMA jobs resumed on that node. No more `adminq timed out` in dmesg for 15m.

kai: Good canary. This points at an interaction between driver v2.4.8 + fw 1.9.0 under heavy east-west GPU traffic (large RDMA scatter/gather). Recommend: 1) hold rollout for rest of x2dn pool, 2) open vendor ticket with logs and `modinfo ena` + `dmesg` + ethtool stats, 3) schedule controlled rollback of driver on a small batch to 2.4.6 to confirm.

sam: I'll file a rollback playbook and temp autoscaler policy to avoid scheduling big RDMA jobs on remaining canaries. Also add a short-term workforce oncall to watch flaps.

nicole: Filing ticket to AWS ENA team with logs + sample pcap attached. Rolling back the driver on two more nodes now to 2.4.6 as experiment.

lina: Once vendor confirms root cause we should add an automatic mitigation to our node bootstrap: on detected `ena_com_adminq` warnings, toggle off GRO/GSO and lower MTU until a safe driver/fw is available. Can make it opt-in via node-label so Dedicated customers can choose.

ops-bot: incident:created #INC-2026-114 (priority:high) assigned to eng-infra.

sam: Thanks team. Keep thread updated. If rollback clears across 5 canaries we can remediatively rollback fleet-wide or wait for vendor patch. :thumbsup:

nicole: Will post post-mortem in #postmortems after closure. For now canary stable.
